purpose: Teach: 泣ける/競っ/上っ/臨む/抜粋/シーツ/出迎え/ハプニング

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと泣ける映画を見たぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Gran, do you remember when we were young and watched that tearjerker with Dad?
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle reach into memory. Warm but searching — not entirely certain she'll recall this moment. Pace unhurried, like letting a old photograph develop.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃同期と競って成績を上げたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and Grandpa, you were always competing with your colleagues back then, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle correction wrapped in affection. A slight tilt of the head — redirecting toward her own memory of him. Warm acknowledgment that he's remembering something different. Not unkind, just... present with her own version.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、出世階段を上っていたぞ、覚えてる?
lines.en: Gran, remember when I was climbing that career ladder in those days?
lines.style: Softer now, more vulnerable. Reaching further back. The tone of someone half-wondering if the memory is still shared, or if it's become his alone. Slight hesitation before 'climbing.'

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、難局に臨むご姿勢、立派だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — the way you faced those difficult times, so dignified, wasn't it, dear?
lines.style: Quiet admiration underneath. She's not answering his question — she's telling him what she saw in him. Direct, gentle, the way you compliment someone by naming what you witnessed. Steady warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、新聞の抜粋を切り抜いてらしたぞ
lines.en: Gran, I used to cut out excerpts from the newspapers back then.
lines.style: Voice grows smaller, more fragmentary. As if following a thread deeper into the past. Matter-of-fact surface, but underneath: wondering if she knows why he did that. Trailing into the memory itself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お布団のシーツ、白がお好きだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you always did prefer white sheets on the futon, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Small, specific detail delivered with absolute certainty. The way people who've lived together fifty years speak — naming the small truths that outlast everything else. Warm, almost playful in its precision.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お客様の出迎えを丁寧になさっていたぞ
lines.en: Gran, you used to welcome guests so carefully, so graciously.
lines.style: Voice steadies slightly. Moving into territory that feels safer — observable, external. Admiration for her in this line. Slower pace on 'graciously.' Letting the memory of her kindness settle.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、思いがけないハプニング、楽しまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and you always loved when something unexpected happened, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warmth with a hint of knowing smile in the voice. A gentle, slightly amused reflection on his nature. The kind of thing you say when you've watched someone for decades embrace small surprises. Soft, close, intimate.
